identity.title: A Survey of C<SUB>2</SUB>H, HCN, and C<SUP>18</SUP>O in Protoplanetary Disks

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present ALMA Band 6 observations of C$_2$H, HCN, and C$^{18}$O in a sample of 14 disks spanning a range of ages, stellar luminosities, and stellar masses.

targets.name: 14 protoplanetary disks (AS 209, CI Tau, DM Tau, DO Tau, HD 143006, HD 163296, IM Lup, J1604-2130, J1609-1908, J1612-1859, J1614-1906, LkCa 15, MWC 480, V4046 Sgr)

evidence.quote: From *Gaia* Data Release 2
From *Gaia* Data Release 2

question.value: How do C2H, HCN and C18O emission, excitation, optical depth and morphology relate to each other and to disk properties (age, luminosity, mass) across 14 protoplanetary disks?

evidence.quote: To this end, we present a survey of C$^{18}$O, C$_2$H, and HCN in 14 protoplanetary disks.
We present ALMA Band 6 observations of C$_2$H, HCN, and C$^{18}$O
Lastly, C$^{18}$O J = 2 – 1 was targeted towards all disks, together with CO J = 2 – 1.
H$^{13}$CN J = 3 – 2 is included for AS 209, CI Tau, DM Tau, DO Tau, HD 163296, LkCa 15, MWC 480, and V4046 Sgr.

baselines.value: 15-705 m for most ALMA programs (21-558 m for 2013.1.00226.S); SMA 16-226 m

pi_or_archival_as_stated.value: Data from various ALMA and SMA programs; C18O described in Huang2017 and J. Pegues (in prep.)

evidence.quote: This project makes use of data from various ALMA and SMA programs, summarized in Table [2](#tab:obsdat).

provided.value: HCN J=3-2 for CI Tau, DM Tau, DO Tau, LkCa 15, MWC 480 (project 2017B-S036)

evidence.quote: CI Tau, DM Tau, DO Tau, LkCa 15, and MWC 480 were observed with the SMA and the remaining disks with ALMA.

what.value: Stellar ages, masses, luminosities of sample

evidence.quote: References: \[1\] (cite: Andrews2009), \[2\] (cite: Guilloteau2014), \[3\] (cite: Andrews2013)

external_data_from_literature.citation: Andrews2009; Guilloteau2014; Andrews2013; Vioque2018 and others (Table 1)

what.value: Disk inclinations and PAs from Keplerian mask fitting to CO

evidence.quote: Derived from Keplerian mask fitting to CO emission (J. Pegues, in preparation)
We adopt a $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C value of 68 $\pm$ 15 appropriate for the local ISM (cite: Milam2005).

what.value: Source-specific disk structure parameters for toy models

evidence.loc: 5.3 C2H morphologies in our disk sample
evidence.quote: The physical structure for each of these disks has been modeled previously in the literature, and we use these constraints to produce toy models for each disk

external_data_from_literature.citation: Table 6 refs (Andrews2009, Oberg2015, Cleeves2016, Andrews2011, Rosenfeld2013a)

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: Toy disk models with RADMC-3D UV flux and atomic carbon distributions (generic and for 6 source-specific disks)

evidence.quote: We use the radiative transfer code RADMC-3D (cite: Dullemond2012) mctherm task to solve for dust temperatures in the disk.
added in quadrature with a 10% calibration uncertainty

self_calibration.value: Phase self-cal on continuum of individual spws, one or two rounds, applied to line data

evidence.quote: One or two rounds of phase self-calibration were performed depending on the continuum brightness.
calibrated and continuum-subtracted data were CLEANed to a 3$\sigma$ noise threshold in CASA 4.6

weighting_robust.value: Briggs robust = 1.0 for line cubes (0.5 for continuum)

evidence.quote: using Briggs weighting with a robust factor of 1.0.

masking.value: Hand-drawn masks for strong emission; 5σ continuum contour for weak lines

evidence.quote: CLEAN masks were drawn by hand for strong emission; for weak lines the 5$\sigma$ continuum contour was used as the CLEAN mask.
The self-calibration solutions were applied to the spectral line data followed by continuum subtraction in the uv plane.

smoothing.value: Channels 0.5 km/s generally; 0.14 km/s for hyperfine fitting cubes

evidence.quote: To produce image cubes for hyperfine fitting a higher spectral resolution of 0.14 km/s was used.

what.value: Keplerian masking method for moment maps, spectra and fluxes

evidence.quote: Our methodology is described in detail in (cite: Bergner2018) and J. Pegues (in preparation).
C$^{18}$O observational details are described in (cite: Huang2017) and J. Pegues (in preparation).
Our fitting procedure is adapted from (cite: Estalella2017) and (cite: Mangum2015).
Our physical model is based on the formalism presented in (cite: Andrews2011) and (cite: Rosenfeld2013)

unstated_but_needed: Exact outer radii used for Keplerian masks per line
Spectral window/line-free channels used for continuum subtraction
Details of SMA tapering for H13CN
UV spectrum scaling and RADMC-3D photon numbers
Filling factor assumption details for HCN beam dilution

analysis_steps.goal: Extract line moment maps, spectra and fluxes

method.value: Keplerian masking of cubes with disk geometry; bootstrapping of uncertainties with 1000 synthetic emission-free cubes

evidence.quote: the same Keplerian mask used to extract line emission is applied to 1000 synthetic image cubes composed of randomly drawn emission-free channels neighboring the target line.

key_parameters.value: Detection: flux >3σ and at least 3 channels >3×rms

evidence.quote: at least 3 channels show emission $>3\times$ rms within the Keplerian mask

analysis_steps.goal: Hyperfine fitting of C2H and HCN spectra per pixel

method.value: Fit hyperfine model spectra in pixels along the major axis to get tau, Tex, column density

evidence.quote: we extract spectra from each pixel within a slice along the disk major axis the width of the beam major axis.

key_parameters.value: Pixels with peak SNR <6 excluded; widths >2.5 km/s and tau outside 0.15-30 excluded

evidence.quote: we exclude pixels with derived optical depths outside the range of 0.15 to 30

assumptions.value: LTE; filling factor 1; Tbg from local continuum brightness temperature

evidence.quote: We note that this fitting assumes LTE conditions

fitting.value: emcee affine-invariant MCMC sampling four parameters ΔV_i, V_lsr, A_m*, tau_m*

evidence.quote: We use the affine-invariant MCMC package emcee (cite: Foreman-Mackey2013) to sample posterior distributions of the four fit parameters.

validation.value: Compared HCN hyperfine result in J1604-2130 with isotopologue results

evidence.quote: this agreement points to the robustness of both methods

analysis_steps.goal: HCN optical depth from HCN/H13CN ratio

method.value: Radially binned integrated intensity ratios with 12C/13C=68

evidence.quote: we instead use the ratio of velocity-integrated intensities, making the assumption that HCN and H$^{13}$CN have similar line profiles

key_parameters.value: Only pixels with H13CN SNR >2.5; H13CN tapered to SMA beam for LkCa 15 and MWC 480

evidence.quote: including only pixels in which the H$^{13}$CN signal to noise ratio is greater than 2.5

assumptions.value: Co-spatial emission; molecular 12C/13C equals atomic ratio

evidence.quote: assuming co-spatial emission of both molecules and that the molecular $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratio is the same as the atomic ratio

method.value: Column density from integrated flux for Tex = 10 and 30 K, with and without optical depth correction (tau=2 C2H, 8 HCN), using radius containing 50% of emission

evidence.quote: we calculate column densities for 10K and 30K excitation temperatures

assumptions.value: tau = 2 for C2H and 8 for HCN

evidence.quote: corrected for an assumed optical depth of 2 for C$_2$H and 8 for HCN

analysis_steps.goal: Toy disk models of UV flux and atomic carbon to explain C2H morphology

method.value: RADMC-3D dust temperature and mcmono UV field; parametrized gas temperature; atomic C where column < f_pen N_diss; overlap profile integral of n_C × F_UV dz compared with observed radial profiles

evidence.quote: we also plot the vertically-integrated convolution of both factors: $\int n_c \times F_{UV} dz$, hereafter referred to as overlap profiles.

key_parameters.value: N_diss = 1.3e21 H2 cm-2; f_pen = f_dep = 1, 10, 100; G0 = 5; dust-to-gas 0.01

evidence.quote: we evaluate atomic carbon abundances for $f_{\mathrm{pen}}$ = $f_{\mathrm{dep}}$ = 1, 10, and 100

validation.value: Qualitative comparison of overlap profile shapes to observed C2H profiles

evidence.quote: The shapes of the modeled overlap profiles and the observed C$_2$H emission profiles generally match well.

method.value: Radex grid for T Tauri and Herbig Ae conditions; Spearman correlation of continuum-normalized fluxes

evidence.quote: We normalize each disk-integrated line flux to the continuum flux in order to cancel out any dependency on the disk angular size.
CLEANed to a 3$\sigma$ noise threshold in CASA 4.6
SMA data were calibrated using the `MIR ` software package
We use the affine-invariant MCMC package emcee (cite: Foreman-Mackey2013)

used_for.value: Dust temperature (mctherm) and UV field (mcmono) in toy models

evidence.quote: We use the radiative transfer code RADMC-3D (cite: Dullemond2012) mctherm task to solve for dust temperatures in the disk.
we run Radex models (cite: Vandertak2007) for a grid of densities and temperatures
calculated using the DIANA project Opacity-Tool (cite: Woitke2016)
C$_2$H is marginally optically thick ($\tau$ $\sim$1–5)
HCN is quite optically thick ($\tau$ $\sim$ 5–10) in the inner 200 AU
Excitation temperatures range from 10 – 40K for C$_2$H, and 5 – 20K for HCN.

results_numeric.quantity: Spearman coefficient C2H vs HCN normalized flux

evidence.quote: for C$_2$H with HCN the coefficient is 0.8 with a p-value of 0.003

results_numeric.quantity: Disk-averaged N(C2H) at 10 K, tau-corrected, sample range

evidence.quote: range from 5 – 37 $\times$ 10$^{12}$ cm$^{-2}$ for C$_2$H

results_numeric.quantity: Disk-averaged N(HCN) at 10 K, tau-corrected, sample range

evidence.quote: from 1 – 10 $\times$ 10$^{12}$ cm$^{-2}$ for HCN

findings_qualitative.value: C2H and HCN fluxes correlate positively; neither correlates with C18O; no age trend

evidence.quote: find a positive correlation between C$_2$H and HCN fluxes, but no relationship between C$_2$H or HCN with C$^{18}$O fluxes.

findings_qualitative.value: HD 163296 C2H column density local minima coincide with planet locations of Teague2018

evidence.quote: the locations of local minima in the column density profile coincide nearly exactly with the locations of planets identified by (cite: Teague2018)

claims.hypothesis: Are C2H and HCN optically thick and cold in disks?
claims.finding: Low temperatures indicate sub-thermal emission from warm atmosphere or beam dilution

evidence.quote: These low temperatures likely result from sub-thermal emission in the warm disk atmosphere, and/or beam dilution due to chemical substructure.

claims.hypothesis: Does overlap of UV flux and atomic carbon explain C2H morphology diversity?
claims.experiment: Toy models for 6 disks, overlap profiles vs observed profiles
claims.result: Overlap profile shapes generally match observations, best with high depletion inner and low outer
claims.finding: UV-atomic C interplay explains compact/extended, ringed/ringless C2H

evidence.quote: the interplay between local UV fluxes and atomic carbon availability is a useful framework that can explain the wide range in observed C$_2$H emission morphologies in our sample.

claims.hypothesis: Do C2H, HCN and C18O share a common oxygen-depletion driver?
claims.experiment: Spearman correlations of continuum-normalized fluxes and age comparison
claims.result: C2H-HCN correlated; none with C18O; no age trend
claims.finding: Common driver for C2H and HCN, but oxygen depletion as driver is questioned

evidence.quote: throw into question whether gas-phase oxygen depletion is a driver of hydrocarbon and cyanide chemistry

claims.hypothesis: Can C2H column density profiles trace planets?
claims.experiment: Compare HD 163296 C2H column profile to planet locations
claims.finding: Possible planet tracer, needs more tests

evidence.quote: HD 163296 is the only disk in our sample with well-detected C$_2$H substructure.

why_this_data.value: Disks chosen to span ages, stellar masses and luminosities

evidence.quote: The target disks were chosen to span a range of ages ($<$1 to $\sim$10 Myr)

limitations_admitted.value: Fluxes may not trace abundances due to optical depth and excitation effects

evidence.quote: an important caveat to this analysis is that fluxes may not be reliable tracers of molecular abundances.

limitations_admitted.value: SMA HCN data poorly resolved, beam dilution

evidence.quote: HCN observations taken with the SMA are not well resolved

referee_caveats_inferred: LTE hyperfine fitting with unresolved structure may bias Tex
Only 14 disks, so correlation significance is limited
Toy models are not full chemistry and parameters are partly adopted from literature
Heterogeneous beams between ALMA and SMA complicate flux comparisons

evidence.quote: This paper makes use of ALMA data, project codes: 2013.1.00226, 2015.1.00671.S, 2015.1.00964.S, and 2016.1.00627.S.

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~100-300 GB raw for four ALMA programs (14 disks, multiple EBs)
